scope: Bounded primary-source consistency review of four overdue Utah statute records (SB 149 2024, SB 226 2025, SB 332 2025, HB 320 2026) against retained enrolled-copy PDFs from le.utah.gov. Owner queue item from the maintenance pilot. No record edits.

method.retrieval: Each enrolled PDF was first downloaded on 2026-09-09 (local) without HTTP metadata being recorded. On 2026-09-10T05:34:50Z all four URLs were re-retrieved with curl -sS -L --max-redirs 3 --max-time 60 -A publedge-source-review/1.0 -w '%{http_code}|%{content_type}|%{url_effective}|%{num_redirects}|%{size_download}'. Every response was HTTP 200, content-type application/pdf, zero redirects, and byte-identical (sha256) to the retained file; the http_status, content_type, final_url, server_last_modified and retrieved_at values below are from that re-retrieval, which is the basis for acquisition primary_retrieval.
method.review_snapshot: pdftotext -layout <pdf> <txt> (poppler 26.08.0), raw output without trimming. On 2026-09-10 a fresh -layout extraction of each retained PDF reproduced the retained .txt byte-for-byte (sha256 equal for all four). SB0332-enrolled.txt is 2679 bytes because the enrolled bill is two pages (pdfinfo Pages: 2); extraction did not fail. Every snapshot begins with an 'Enrolled Copy' header naming the expected bill number. The pre-existing data/admission/sources/utah-hb452/HB0452-enrolled.txt (already tracked) differs from raw -layout output only by stripped leading whitespace on line 1 and the trailing form-feed/newline; it was not modified.
method.url_checks: One HTTP HEAD request per unique https URL appearing in the four records (frontmatter and body), run 2026-09-10T05:35:35Z to 05:35:40Z with curl -sS -I --max-time 30; no retries, no GET fallback. Schema and w3id ontology URLs (200 and 303 respectively) are not source documents and are omitted from the per-record lists.
method.locators: Line references are the enrolled bill's own left-margin line numbers as printed in the reviewed UTF-8 snapshot; page references are the enrolled PDF's printed page numbers.
method.effective_date_basis: All four enrolled bills carry their own effective-date section (SB 149 Section 13; SB 226 Section 9; SB 332 Section 2; HB 320 Section 8), so the Utah default of 60 days after sine die was not needed for any record.

confirmed: Title 'Artificial Intelligence Amendments' and '2024 GENERAL SESSION' match the record title and session (page 1, lines 1-3).
Effective date: Section 13 'This bill takes effect on May 1, 2024.' matches effective 2024-05-01 (page 18, line 593).

Section 1 enacts 13-2-12 (generative AI disclosure; on-request trigger 'if asked or prompted', regulated-occupation 'prominently disclose'), matching the record's §13-2-12 anchor and Summary (lines 39-41, 73-76).

Section 12 enacts 76-2-107 'Commission of offense with aid of generative artificial intelligence', matching the §76-2-107 anchor and the ai-defense-elimination obligation's criminal prong (lines 584-591).

Annual report before November 30 to the Business and Labor Interim Committee (line 465) supports the report milestones used in the SB 226 and HB 320 records.

findings.record_value: Utah Code Title 13, Chapter 72 (Artificial Intelligence Policy Act)
findings.source_value: The enrolled bill enacts 13-70-101 through 13-70-305 and its sunset clause names 'Title 13, Chapter 70, Artificial Intelligence Act' (Sections Affected lines 29-35; Section 11 line 583). The long title calls the act the 'Artificial Intelligence Policy Act' (line 5). The Chapter 72 numbering is the codified location (HB 320 cites '13-72-101, as enacted by Laws of Utah 2024, Chapter 186').
findings.assessment: Locator note, not a falsity. The record cites the codified chapter, which is correct for current Utah Code, but the enrolled text uses Chapter 70. A human editor may want a note that the enrolled bill numbered the chapter 13-70 before codification.

findings.field: body Summary bullet 'SB 332 extended the Chapter 72 sunset from 2025-07-01 to 2027-07-01'
findings.source_value: SB 149 Section 11 sets the repeal date at May 1, 2025 (line 583); SB 332 Section 1 strikes 'May' and '2025' and inserts 'July 1, 2027' (SB 332 lines 30-31).
findings.locator: SB 149 page 18 line 583; SB 332 page 2 lines 30-31
findings.assessment: Discrepancy. The original sunset was 2025-05-01, not 2025-07-01. The record's own Timeline row for SB 332 and the SB 332 record both use 2025-05-01 correctly; only this Summary bullet is wrong.

findings.field: body Summary bullet 'HB 320 (2026) ... extended the maximum agreement term from 12 to 36 months'
findings.source_value: SB 149 Section 10 (13-70-305) allowed an initial 12-month agreement plus 'a single 12-month extension' (lines 572-575), so the pre-HB 320 maximum was 24 months.
findings.assessment: Discrepancy in the starting figure. The 36-month ceiling after HB 320 is confirmed by HB 320 Section 6; the prior ceiling was 24 months, not 12.

retained_sources.document_title: Artificial Intelligence Consumer Protection Amendments, Enrolled Copy

confirmed: Title 'Artificial Intelligence Consumer Protection Amendments' and '2025 GENERAL SESSION' match (page 1, lines 1-3).
Effective date: Section 9(1) 'this bill takes effect on May 7, 2025' and every enacted 13-75 section is marked '(Effective 05/07/25)', matching effective 2025-05-07 (page 6, line 188; lines 27-34).

Enacts 13-75-101 through 13-75-106 and repeals 13-2-12 'as enacted by Laws of Utah 2024, Chapter 186' (lines 26-34, 183-186), matching the record's Chapter 75 anchors and the SB 149 record's 'repealed by SB 226' note.

§13-75-103(1)(b) 'clear and unambiguous request' trigger (lines 103-105); §13-75-103(2)-(3) proactive verbal/written disclosure for high-risk interactions in regulated occupations (lines 106-115); §13-75-104 outset-and-throughout safe harbor (lines 117-126); §13-75-101(5) high-risk definition covering health, financial, biometric data and financial, legal, medical, mental health advice (lines 54-67); §13-75-102 'not a defense' civil rule (lines 90-95). All match the Summary and the mapped obligations disclose-genai-on-request, disclose-genai-high-risk-proactive, and ai-defense-elimination.
Amends relationship to SB 149 is supported by the repeal of 13-2-12 and the definitional cross-reference to 13-72-101 (line 40-41).

findings.field: effective and Timeline note 'Default 2025 session effective date'
findings.record_value: 2025-05-07 (described as the default session effective date)
findings.source_value: Line 12: 'This bill provides a special effective date.' Section 2: 'This bill takes effect: (1) except as provided in Subsection (2), May 7, 2025; or (2) if approved by two-thirds of all members elected to each house: (a) upon approval by the governor; ...' (page 2, lines 32-39).
findings.assessment: Discrepancy to resolve. The bill carries a two-thirds trigger, not a plain default date. The record's own Timeline reports Senate 24-0-5 and House 74-0-1; if those vote counts are accurate they exceed two-thirds of each house (29 and 75 members), which would make the bill effective on governor approval (record enacted 2025-03-25) rather than 2025-05-07. Vote counts are not in the enrolled copy, so a human editor must confirm the passage votes on le.utah.gov before changing the effective date. Left unchanged.

findings.field: body Summary and Talking Point exclusivity ('Its sole AI-relevant effect', 'the statutory reason ... still exist', 'Without SB 332 ... would have sunset on May 1, 2025')
findings.record_value: SB 332 presented as the sole extension of the Chapter 72 sunset
findings.source_value: SB 226 (2025) Section 7 makes the identical amendment to 63I-2-213(5) (SB 226 lines 169-182, 187-195). SB 332's own text is consistent with the record, but the exclusivity framing is not supported once SB 226 is read.
findings.assessment: Overstatement for a human editor to weigh. The extension itself (to 2027-07-01) is correctly recorded.

retained_sources.document_title: Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy Amendments, Enrolled Copy

confirmed: Bill number H.B. 320 and '2026 GENERAL SESSION' match (page 1, lines 1-3).
Effective date: Section 8 'This bill takes effect on May 6, 2026.' matches effective 2026-05-06 (page 8, line 250). 'Other Special Clauses: None' (line 17).

Joint interpretation agreement defined at 13-72-101(12) and governed by 13-72-401 (Part 4, lines 164-212); participant 'remains subject to all legal and regulatory requirements not expressly waived ... or clarified in a joint interpretation agreement' (lines 193-195), matching the no-waiver characterization.
'Governmental entity' means the judiciary, state-funded higher or public education institutions, or a political subdivision (13-72-101(10), lines 54-57), matching the expanded-counterparties bullet.
13-72-401(6) 'The office shall perform regular audits' (lines 190-192) matches the mandatory-audits bullet.
13-72-402(1)(a)-(e) five eligibility prongs (lines 217-228) match the five-prong bullet and the learning-lab-agreement-participation obligation's What Counts list.
13-72-403: initial demonstration period may not exceed 12 months, 12-month extensions, 'up to two extensions' (lines 236-245), matching the 36-month ceiling.

13-72-201(3)(d) annual report before November 30 now includes executed regulatory mitigation or joint interpretation agreements (lines 111-117), supporting the 'Second annual report 2026-11-30' milestone.
HB 320 does not touch 63I-2-213, consistent with the SB 332 record's statement that HB 320 did not alter the sunset date.

findings.record_value: Utah HB 320 (2026) — AI Learning Lab Restructure + Joint Interpretation Agreements
findings.source_value: Enrolled short title: 'Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy Amendments' (page 1, line 1).
findings.assessment: Editorial title differs from the enrolled short title. The SB 149, SB 226, and SB 332 records use the enrolled short title; this one does not. Not a factual error, but inconsistent with sibling records.

findings.field: body Summary bullet 'The maximum agreement term was extended from 12 months (with no renewal) to 12 months plus two 12-month extensions'
findings.source_value: Prior 13-72-305 text, shown struck in Section 6: 'A participant may request a [single ]12-month [extension ...]' (lines 236-241), i.e. one renewal was already allowed (24-month maximum). SB 149 lines 572-575 confirm the original single extension.
findings.assessment: Discrepancy. The prior ceiling was 12 months plus one 12-month extension, not 'no renewal'.

findings.field: obligation learning-lab-agreement-participation, Statute Anchors: 'Utah Code §13-72-301 — Joint Interpretation Agreements (added by HB 320, 2026)'
findings.source_value: Section 3 amends 13-72-301 'Artificial Intelligence Learning Laboratory Program' (lines 120-121); joint interpretation agreements are in 13-72-401 (Part 4, lines 164-166) and defined at 13-72-101(12).
findings.assessment: Discrepancy in the obligation record's anchor label (data/examples/obligations/learning-lab-agreement-participation.md). The mapping hb320-joint-interpretation-agreements points this obligation at the HB 320 record.

admission.note: Unchanged from baseline. Retained sources were added under data/admission/sources without any record change, so no admission receipt was created or altered; the four records remain legacy-unreviewed.

limits: Statutory interpretation and the Utah statutory spine are owned by EveryAILaw (https://everyailaw.com/regulation/utah-sb149/); this review checks PubLedge record text against enrolled bill text only and makes no legal conclusion.

This is an agent source-consistency review. It does not renew last_verified, status, editorial_status, modified, or any legal-status field on any record; all four records keep last_verified 2026-06-04 and remain overdue under the 90-day cadence.
Overdue is not proof of a false record. The findings above are candidate corrections for a human editor, recorded with locators; none has been applied.
Enrolled copies do not show governor signing dates, passage votes, or later codification; those record fields were neither confirmed nor contradicted.
Codified Utah Code text was not retrieved; section URLs were only HEAD-checked once each, and a 404 on HEAD was not retried with GET.

No publication, deployment, push, pull request, package version change, or provider mutation was performed. Only public le.utah.gov, everyailaw.com, and commerce.utah.gov endpoints were contacted; no paid provider was used.
